editorial:
Imagine waking up in modern Berlin with no memory of how you got there, only to discover you are Adolf Hitler. That is the wild setup of this dark German comedy. Hitler stumbles into present-day life, meets a struggling filmmaker named Fabian, and the two hit the road. People assume he is a brilliant method actor or comedian, and soon he is a TV star. The vibe is sharp and uncomfortable, mixing real street reactions with scripted scenes. You will laugh, then feel uneasy about laughing.

The acting is strong, especially the lead who nails Hitler's mannerisms without turning him into a cartoon. The pacing moves fast, though the road-trip middle can drag a bit. The biggest pro is how it makes you think about media and fame; the con is that the satire sometimes hits too close to home. If you enjoy bold, thought-provoking comedy, this is for you. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your shelf.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Hitler is shot by a woman whose grandmother was murdered by the Nazis. He survives and wakes up in a hospital bed, eyes open and already planning his next move. The twist is that the public never truly rejected him; the film shows real people agreeing with his views, suggesting his ideas still find an audience today. It ends on a chilling note rather than a clean victory.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves bold satire and dark comedy.
